As a non beginner I think the most important things are finding the angle,

Lay the blade flat horiziotal against the stone with the blade towards you, then raise the blade until the shadow disappears and the blade edge is flush and tight to the stone, that is the angle you want to sharpen at.

Understanding the Burr is also important, its the thin wire-like trim that affixes to the tip of the blade while sharpening sharpening is low scale grinding the metal to get rid of any dings chips and folds in the edge, that metal attaches itself to the very tip of the blade, you can't really see if very good but you can feel it with your fingernail, sharpen until you have a consistent burr all the way down the blade. At this point you can drag the blade softly crossgrain against some denim(your leg in jeans) in each direction to break off the burr, then you should have a decent edge. That's "sharpening"

The next step is honing (smoothing the edge) for this you want a steel or even better ceramic honing rod, run the blade lightly once each way 5 or 6 times each at a slightly steeper angle then the stone, you shouldn't need too much on the ceramic, all it's doing is getting rid of some micro bits of the burr and straightening/smoothing out the edge, check it with your fingernail, if you feel any resistence do a few more swipes. This will get your knife really sharp and perfectly usable. BUT there's more magic to be done.

Get a piece of leather and glue it rough side up to a piece of wood to make a "Strop" and buy and rub some stropping compound (or toothpaste if you don't mind the smell) and drag the blade backards and any and every angle up to the blades bevel and you can achieve a mirror polished edge that will cut any paper, shave any hair.
